Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

HowMaHiCo 0.22.0

PEAKS Xpro actually works now

Verifying the PEAKS claim with a shipped dataset (Tier C’s last item) turned up two bugs that made the documented PEAKS entry point unusable, both silent or cryptic rather than loud:

  • read_peaks_batch() filtered the export FOLDERS by the PER-SAMPLE key. A PEAKS export folder normally holds several samples, one Area#<sample> column each inside its peptide.csv, and [read_peaks()] turns those suffixes into Sample_peaks – which is also what annotate_peaks() joins the metadata on. Filtering folders by that same value therefore matched no folder at all whenever folder and sample names differed (i.e. always, for a multi-sample export): the empty read then died inside parse_peaks() with object 'Accession' not found. Keying the annotation on the folder instead produced the mirror failure – a silent 0-row join. Folder selection now uses Sample_folder (falling back to Sample_peaks for the one-folder-per-sample layout, where the two coincide), and both halves of the trap now fail with an error naming the two keys and showing what was found on each side.
  • read_peaks_batch() pasted an absolute path behind the working directory. It called read_peaks(filedir = getwd(), folder_peaks_db = <indexed path>), so an absolute FolderData – exactly what the reports document and what system.file() returns – became an unopenable path. It now splits the indexed path with dirname()/basename(), which reconstructs a relative or absolute path unchanged.
  • get_annot_peaks() documents that one row per folder is not one row per sample, and what to add by hand for a multi-sample export.

A simulated PEAKS export to test against

  • New inst/extdata/sim_peaks_xpro/ (+ sim_peaks_xpro_annotation.csv): the 462 simulated peptides over 6 samples in real PEAKS Xpro shape – one export folder, -10lgP, a 1/k0 Range string, Area#<sample> columns, a few oxidised methionines written PEAKS-style ((+15.99) on the peptide, the name in PTM). PEAKS was the only engine with no end-to-end fixture, which is why the above went unnoticed. ~61 KB.
  • test-loaders-peaks.R gained the end-to-end build_pep_all("peaks_xpro") assertion, a check that folder selection keys on Sample_folder, and a check that each half of the key mix-up now errors loudly.

Corrected PTM documentation

  • v0.19.0 described PEAKS as writing a bracketed delta mass in PTM. It does not: PEAKS writes the modification name (Oxidation (M)) and keeps the delta mass in the peptide string. translate_ptm() handled this correctly already – a token with no number falls through unchanged – but the docs, the two report notes and the test comments said otherwise, and are now right. A test pins the pass-through so a PEAKS name can never be mangled into a mass match.

The abstract

  • example/abstract_eupa2026_v3.md now names what the code does: motif clarity is attributed to anchor information content for class 1 and nested binding cores for class 2, and the identification-QC sentence distinguishes DDA mass error from DIA retention-time/ion-mobility calibration error.

HowMaHiCo 0.21.0

Interactive plots, on a toggle

  • New param InteractivePlots (default FALSE), declared by all ten templates. With TRUE the convertible plots become plotly widgets – hover values, zoom, pan – instead of static images, which is what the reports’ “interactive HTML” claim should mean beyond tabsets and DT tables.
  • ggprint_rawr() gained an interactive argument returning plotly::ggplotly(input). It keeps the caller-frame name resolution and the not-generated guard, so the 34 call sites that already used it needed one argument each and nothing else. The shared setup (and the two 00_* templates, which do not use it) derives interactive_plots <- isTRUE(params$InteractivePlots) once.
  • Plots inside results='asis' tabset loops are deliberately left static. An htmlwidget printed from such a loop needs an explicit tagList/knit_print dance to get its dependencies attached and otherwise renders empty, with no error – the same reason those loops already use kable rather than DT. A new test walks every skeleton’s chunks and fails if an asis chunk ever asks for an interactive plot.
  • Unconvertible objects are returned unchanged, never converted and never erroring: ggpubr composites (plot_peplength_dens(), plot_pepmass()), sequence logos, and anything that is already a widget (.ggplotly_incompatible). Asking for interactivity cannot break a report.
  • The three bare plot prints in 05_quality_score and the four ggplotly() calls on the log2(Area) correlation matrices now route through the same helper. The correlation matrices pass interactive = TRUE unconditionally, preserving the always-interactive behaviour they have had since v0.1.

Tests

  • test-sim-fragpipe.R renders 05_quality_score against the simulated data with the toggle on and off and asserts that the widget containers and the embedded plotly library are present in one and absent in the other. Rendering is the only way to catch the silent-empty-widget failure – no parse check or unit test can see it.
  • test-theme-and-save.R covers the conversion, the preserved default, the not-generated guard under interactive = TRUE, and the pass-through of a ggpubr composite / a non-plot / an object that is already a widget.
  • test-report-templates.R gained the asis-boundary guard above, the InteractivePlots entry in its common_params list, and a check that a template using interactive_plots really derives it.

HowMaHiCo 0.20.0

A motif dimension for MHC class II

  • New metric frac_nested_core in qc_metrics_by_sample(), with the internal .nested_core_fraction(). For MHCclass = "MHC2" both frac_9mer and anchor_information are NA – class-II ligands have no fixed-length anchor register – so the quality score had no motif dimension at all for the class the package’s title claims to support. Class-II peptides are trimmed into ragged, length-variable families around one ~9-residue binding core, so this measures the fraction of in-window ligands sharing a 9-mer with another ligand of the same sample. No alignment, register guess, binding predictor or external data is involved.
  • quality_thresholds_default("MHC2") promotes it to the anchor metric’s weight
    1. and relabels it “Nested-core families”; for MHC1/MHC1_mouse it stays a weight-0 diagnostic, since some nesting is normal there but is not the primary signal. Metric keys are identical across classes, as with the mouse frac_9mer rewrite. The class-II cut-offs are provisional – prefer ThresholdMode = "qc_relative".
  • It is computed on the in-window ligands only, so a long tryptic tail cannot manufacture nesting, and a sequence can never count as nested with itself (one (k-mer, sequence) pair at most, so internal repeats do not register).

Identification QC that works for DIA

  • New metrics median_abs_rt_error and median_abs_im_error. Mass error is an MS2-level DDA metric: DIA-NN’s Precursor.Mz is the library value and report.tsv carries no observed precursor m/z, so no real ppm can be recovered from it (ppm is a hardcoded dummy, dropped from the score). DIA-NN does report a predicted RT and ion mobility per precursor, and the deviation from them is the DIA analogue – both columns were already carried into pep_all by parse_diann() and unused until now.
  • Both are NA for FragPipe and PEAKS, which carry no prediction, so they drop out of the composite exactly as ppm drops out for DIA-NN. The internal .median_abs_delta() also returns NA when every difference is 0, so a placeholder column cannot score as perfect accuracy. Their cut-offs are instrument- and gradient-dependent, which the report states.
  • 05_quality_score’s Methods section documents both substitutions, and its overview text now names them instead of only listing what drops out.

Tests

  • test-quality-score.R gained the nested-core maths (shared cores, the internal-repeat trap, the NA cases), the per-class threshold promotion, the .median_abs_delta() guards, calibration metrics with and without predictions, and a guard that every scored threshold row exists in the metrics table for every MHC class – a mismatch there would abort the whole report inside score_sample_quality()’s composite step.

HowMaHiCo 0.19.0

Readable PTM names

  • New R/ptm.R: ptm_reference() + translate_ptm(). The PTM column is written differently by every search engine – DIA-NN stores UniMod accessions ((UniMod:35)), FragPipe a delta mass behind a position+residue prefix (2M(15.9949)), PEAKS a signed delta mass rounded to two decimals ([+15.99]) – so the PTM heatmaps showed three unrelated-looking labels for what is one modification, and a UniMod-only translation would have been a silent no-op on the project’s default FragPipe data. translate_ptm() handles all three dialects in one pass and returns Oxidation for each.
  • plot_ptm_heatmap() gained translate = TRUE (and a reference pass-through), applied where the multi-PTM strings are already split into one token per row so both the count and the proportion branch inherit it. translate = FALSE restores the raw engine tokens. Display-time only: pep_all$PTM keeps the raw value, as with the v0.12.0 “data keys unchanged” renames.
  • Unmatched tokens are returned unchanged rather than becoming NA, so an unknown modification stays visible on the heatmap. ptm_reference() is ordered by how commonly each modification occurs, because a few are mass-degenerate (Glu->pyro-Glu/Dehydrated, Gln->pyro-Glu/Ammonia-loss) and the first row within tolerance wins; pass a reordered copy to change that preference.
  • Fixed a factually wrong note in 00_mhc_report and 01_id_counts, which told the reader that “Fragpipe and DIA-NN” numbers are UniMod codes. FragPipe and PEAKS report delta masses; only DIA-NN reports UniMod.

One glossary, generated from one function

  • New pep_all_glossary() (R/report-helpers.R) documents all 30 core pep_all columns, including the caveats that are easy to misread: DIA-NN’s ppm is a hardcoded dummy, its Mass is computed rather than observed, Accession is a protein group only for DIA-NN and PEAKS, and Score is not comparable across engines.
  • New shared child inst/rmarkdown/shared/glossary.Rmd, included by all ten templates ahead of their “Session & provenance” footer. It explains the counting units (peptides vs sequences vs parent proteins vs selected) with the length window interpolated from shortpep_range, then renders pep_all_glossary() as a table.
  • This replaces the hardcoded glossary prose in 00_mhc_report, which had gone stale – it stated a 12-20 AA MHC-II window (the actual window is 12-25) and named 3_results/4_figures regardless of the run’s actual path params. The README gained the same table under a new “Glossary” heading, closing the standby item for it.

Tests

  • New tests/testthat/test-ptm.R: all three token dialects, the tolerance that still separates Acetyl (42.010565) from Trimethyl (42.046950), PEAKS’ 2-decimal rounding, pass-through of unknown tokens/NA/"", the reference-order rule for mass-degenerate modifications, and a plot_ptm_heatmap(translate = TRUE/FALSE) assertion on the plot data.
  • test-report-helpers.R gained two glossary guards: every column validate_pep_all() requires must be documented, and so must every column the reports consume from a real build_pep_all() run on the shipped sim data.

HowMaHiCo 0.18.0

Protein-level table and report

  • New 08_prot_all report and R/prot-all.R engine. Every other report is peptide-centric; protein information existed only as n_Proteins columns inside the ID-count tables and two protein x sample log2 matrices written under CsvSave. build_prot_all() now condenses pep_all to one row per (protein, Sample): ligands contributed, summed intensity, unique-peptide counts, and the protein annotation. It is written to <Subset>_prot_all.csv on every run.
  • Area is summed on the linear scale within a sample and log2’d afterwards, as build_quant_matrix() does. Note the older protein matrices in 00_mhc_report/04_quant take a different route — get_mat_log2area() averages Log2Area — so those numbers are not comparable with these.
  • The protein key is a parameter, because Accession is a protein group only for DIA-NN (a ;-list) and PEAKS (a :-list) — FragPipe puts a single sp|ID|ENTRY string there. ProteinFeature accepts ProteinFirst (default), GeneFirst or Accession.
  • MultiMapping chooses how a shared ligand is counted. A short non-tryptic HLA peptide often maps to several proteins and neither convention is right: "leading" (default) counts it once so per-protein counts still reconcile with the peptide count, "all" counts it for every candidate. expand_mapped_proteins() resolves the engine-specific mapped-protein column (FragPipe Mapped_Proteins, DIA-NN/PEAKS Accession, each with its own separator) by dispatching on Found_By, and warns and falls back to leading when the table carries no such list.
  • n_Peptides_unique finally uses Is_Unique (FragPipe) and Proteotypic (DIA-NN) — both have been carried into pep_all since the loaders were written and were never read.
  • New exports: build_prot_all(), summarise_prot_all(), top_source_proteins(), expand_mapped_proteins(), prot_engine_columns(), diann_protein_columns(), plus plot_proteins_per_sample(), plot_peptides_per_protein(), plot_top_proteins(), plot_protein_detection() and plot_ligand_vs_protein_quant().

Protein data the search engine already reported

  • DIA-NN’s protein-group quantities and q-values are now carried through rather than only recomputed from peptides. PG.MaxLFQ, PG.Quantity, Genes.MaxLFQ, PG.Q.Value and relatives have been sitting in pep_all unused; prot_engine_columns() finds whichever are present and build_prot_all() carries them by a unique-within-group rule — a value that genuinely varies within a group (which happens legitimately when grouping by GeneFirst) becomes NA and is counted in an attribute, never averaged or silently first-picked.
  • plot_ligand_vs_protein_quant() plots summed ligand Area against the engine’s own protein quantity with a Spearman correlation. A weak correlation is the expected result: HLA presentation is shaped by processing and binding, so the plot shows the report’s central caveat instead of only asserting it.
  • Fixed: parse_diann() could drop protein quantities, or refuse to parse at all. Its select() was a bare-name whitelist of ~45 columns, so a report missing any one of them errored, and newer DIA-NN releases — which renamed these fields (PG.Quantity to PG.Abundance, PG.Normalised to PG.NormalisedAbundance) — had their protein quantities silently discarded before reaching pep_all. The protein/gene-level names now go through dplyr::any_of(diann_protein_columns()), so either naming generation survives.
  • FragPipe’s psm.tsv reports no protein quantity (it lives in protein.tsv, which this package does not read) and PEAKS’ peptide export reports none, so the report’s search-engine section degrades to a note naming what does report it.

Scope and caveats

The report is deliberately descriptive — no differential testing, since 06_quant_stats already accepts QuantFeature = "ProteinFirst" — and carries a Methods section stating that summed ligand intensity is not protein abundance, that there is no length normalisation (which needs the search FASTA, still deferred), that protein inference is weak for short non-tryptic peptides, and that its protein count need not match 01_id_counts, which counts n_distinct(Accession).

Also

  • Fixed: docs/ was missing from .Rbuildignore, so R CMD check raised a “non-standard file/directory found at top level” note for anyone who had built the pkgdown site locally.
  • tests/testthat/test-prot-all.R covers the aggregation rules on hand-built fixtures — the shipped simulated dataset has a blank Mapped Proteins column in every row and the make_diann_report_raw() helper sets every PG.* column to NA, so neither multi-mapping nor the engine passthrough can be exercised against them. Two render tests cover 08_prot_all end to end, including that MultiMapping = "all" degrades cleanly when nothing is mapped.

HowMaHiCo 0.17.0

Reports are no longer branded to one platform

  • New optional Provider report param, declared by all nine templates. The header attribution used to be hardcoded into every skeleton (“provided by the Immunopeptidomics Platform (IPP)”), along with a personal @dkfz.de contact block and a **Code author:** DGZ line in the two 00_* reports — so every report rendered by anyone was attributed to one lab. The attribution is now rendered from the param by the new exported provider_line() (R/report-helpers.R), which returns a generic sentence naming no organisation when Provider is empty (the default).
  • The helper is called namespaced, `r HowMaHiCo::provider_line(params$Provider)`: in 00_mhc_report and 00_mhc_upsets the header sits above their inline setup chunk, so the package is not attached when the inline expression evaluates.
  • 00_mhc_upsets gained the description and **Code version:** lines it was missing — the nine headers are now uniform for the first time.

A runnable on-ramp

  • New inst/scripts/howmahico_pipeline.R + exported get_pipeline_script() — a commented walkthrough from raw search output to rendered reports, copied into the working directory the same way get_report_template() and get_dictionary_template() hand out their files. It renders through run_howmahico_report() rather than asking the reader to open a template and knit it by hand.
  • It starts in demo mode: sourced as-is it runs the whole pipeline against the simulated dataset in inst/extdata/sim_fragpipe_dda, so a fresh install can be exercised before any real data is involved.
  • The package’s first vignette (vignettes/howmahico.Rmd, VignetteBuilder: knitr) narrates the same walkthrough and gives the pkgdown site an Articles tab. Its pipeline chunks are eval = FALSE, but the annotation/build_pep_all() section really runs against the simulated data, so the article cannot silently rot.

README

  • Fixed: the headline run_howmahico_report() example could not be run. It passed Title = ..., which no template declares, and rmarkdown errors on an undeclared param ("render params not declared in YAML") — so copy-pasting the primary documented entry point failed outright.
  • Added a Quickstart, a table of what each of the nine reports produces, a full parameter reference (common, focused-only, and the per-report sets for 05, 06 and 07), an output section naming the always-written files and the CsvSave/PlotsSave tiers, and a troubleshooting table. Users are no longer sent to CLAUDE.md, which is maintainer-facing.
  • Corrected stale claims: 07_pepchem was missing from every template list, “mid-conversion, on the dev branch”, “~40 functions” (there are 118 exports), the numbered project folders presented as repository contents, and RStudio listed as a requirement rather than pandoc.

Guards

  • test-report-templates.R now checks that every shipped template declares the common param set, and that no template hardcodes an organisation, author or contact address. A param added to eight of nine templates is not a soft failure: render() stops outright when a caller passes a param the template does not declare.
  • test-get-pipeline-script.R covers the copy/overwrite behaviour, parse()s the shipped script so it cannot rot into a syntax error, and asserts every template name it mentions is still offered by run_howmahico_report().
  • test-sim-fragpipe.R renders with and without Provider and checks the rendered HTML in both directions — a declared-but-unused param would otherwise pass a YAML-only check while changing nothing.

HowMaHiCo 0.16.1

  • Fixed: the pkgdown site had not deployed since v0.8.0. pkgdown aborts the whole build when an exported function is missing from the _pkgdown.yml reference index, and three release cycles (v0.9.0-v0.13.0) added exports without indexing them: the dictionary-driven parser family (parse_unified(), read_dictionary(), read_custom_batch(), annotate_unified(), get_dictionary_template()), the quality-score engine (score_sample_quality() and friends, plus plot_quality_heatmap(), plot_quality_composite(), plot_cross_class_length()) and plot_pseudomobilogram(). All 15 are now indexed, in two new reference sections plus one insertion.
  • New guard tests/testthat/test-pkgdown-index.R. devtools::check() never reads _pkgdown.yml, and the pkgdown workflow only runs on master, so the failure could only be discovered after a merge. The suite now checks that every getNamespaceExports() entry appears in the index, that no index entry names a function that is not exported (a rename or removal breaks the build the same way), and that nothing is listed twice. _pkgdown.yml is .Rbuildignored, so the test locates it by walking up from the test directory and skips when no source tree is reachable.

HowMaHiCo 0.16.0

  • New report 07_pepchem + engine R/pepchem.R: peptide physicochemical properties compared between Conditions. Where the other reports describe which peptides were found, this one describes what they are made of: amino-acid composition (overall, per sample, and as log2 enrichment against the pooled composition of the subset), per-position residue frequency at the dominant peptide length plus an N-/C-terminal profile resolved across all lengths, and per-peptide descriptors — GRAVY, pI, net Charge, MW, Boman, HydrophobicMoment, InstabilityIndex, AliphaticIndex and the amino-acid class fractions.
  • The unit of analysis is the sample, not the peptide. Descriptors are computed once over the unique sequences and attached to each sample that identified them; each sample is summarised first (pepchem_by_sample() -> summarise_pepchem() -> aggregate_pepchem()) and Conditions are then compared across samples. Peptides within a Condition are not independent replicates, so pooling them would return enormous nominal significance for effects carried by one sample.
  • Two comparison tracks, both labelled. compare_pepchem(level = "sample") is the primary, replicate-respecting test (Kruskal-Wallis + pairwise Wilcoxon, BH-corrected within each contrast, with MedianDiff and the new scale-free cliffs_delta() as effect sizes) — and is deliberately low-powered: on 3 vs 3 samples a two-sided Wilcoxon cannot reach p < 0.1, the same structural limit 06_quant_stats documents for its Fisher track. level = "peptide" pools the repertoire and is reported alongside as explicitly descriptive. compare_aa_frequency() applies the same machinery per residue to per-sample frequencies rather than a chi-square on pooled residue counts.
  • New exports: peptide_properties(), pepchem_properties(), aa_composition(), aa_position_frequency(), pepchem_by_sample(), summarise_pepchem(), aggregate_pepchem(), cliffs_delta(), compare_pepchem(), compare_aa_frequency(), plus plot_aa_composition(), plot_aa_position_heatmap(), plot_property_distribution(), plot_property_sample_summary() and plot_property_effectsize() in R/plots.R.
  • aa_position_frequency() generalises the per-position frequency table that anchor_information_content() collapses to Shannon bits, and the two now share the alphabet and the negative-position helper (-1 = C-terminus) instead of keeping duplicate copies.
  • New dependency: Peptides (CRAN, GPL-2, Rcpp only) in Imports — it is vectorised and is the canonical implementation of GRAVY (mean Kyte-Doolittle), so the scales are not re-derived. Peptides::aaComp() is not used (it returns a per-sequence list); the class fractions are derived from the composition matrix. Its per-descriptor “unrecognized amino acid types” warnings are consolidated into one peptide_properties() warning naming the count.
  • Peptide position within the parent protein — the third part of the original request — is deferred; no loader carries a position column, so it needs a user-supplied search FASTA. The design is recorded under Deferred designs in CLAUDE.md.

Fixes found while verifying the new report

  • Fixed: PlotsSave = TRUE never saved anything, and ggprint_rawr() silently dropped plots. Both helpers resolved the plot name with a bare exists(deparse(substitute(input))), which searches from the helper’s own frame outwards through its lexical parents — the HowMaHiCo namespace, then globalenv() — and so never reaches a report’s knit environment (rmarkdown::render() knits in new.env(parent = globalenv())). Every lookup from a report therefore failed: ggsave_rawr() warned and wrote no png, and ggprint_rawr() returned the warning string instead of the plot, which warning = FALSE chunks then swallowed. The name is now resolved in the calling frame via the shared internal .plot_was_built(), and a non-symbol argument (plots[[nm]], the export-loop idiom used by 06 and 07) is evaluated and judged by value, so a NULL plot is skipped rather than saved. On the simulated dataset 07_pepchem goes from 8 to 14 figures and from 0 to 14 saved pngs; 04_quant, 05_quality_score and 06_quant_stats recover their PlotsSave output too.
  • Fixed: 05_quality_score could not render at all. An inline `r ...` expression ended in a bare comma-separated string list (else "a ", "<code>", params$QCColumn, "</code> b") instead of a paste0() call — a syntax error, so the template aborted at the inline-parse stage. The report had never rendered and nothing caught it, because the suite only rendered 01 and 06; test-sim-fragpipe.R now carries a render guard for 05 (which also asserts that PlotsSave writes files and that figures reach the HTML).

HowMaHiCo 0.15.0

  • Mouse MHC-I support. MHCclass accepts a new value "MHC1_mouse" (7-11 AAs, the murine H-2 ligand window) alongside "MHC1" (8-13) and "MHC2" (12-25). The windows and their palettes now come from two exported helpers, mhc_length_window() and mhc_class_palette() (R/report-helpers.R), instead of three copy-pasted lists in the skeletons and a fourth inside the quality-score engine.
  • Quality score is mouse-aware: for "MHC1_mouse" the canonical-length metric counts 8- and 9-mers (H-2Kb favours 8-mers, H-2Db 9-mers) with the label “8/9-mer fraction” and raised green/amber cut-offs (quality_thresholds_default() gained an mhcclass argument); the anchor motif is scored on whichever of the two lengths the sample has more of; the cross-class window follows the 7-11 window. The metric keys are unchanged.
  • Fixed: a single-Condition subset aborted every report. combn(conditions, 2) errors with n < m; the new exported condition_pairs() returns an empty list instead (and self = TRUE gives the overlap matrix its diagonal), and the skeletons use it. Guarded by an end-to-end single-Condition render test.
  • Fixed: an all-zero Area dataset aborted the render. get_mat_log2area() now returns a well-formed 0 x n matrix with a warning when every ID is a phantom, and the correlation chunks of 04_quant / 00_mhc_report test for that before calling cor() (which errors with 'x' is empty) and before computing the colour limits.
  • TestMode now builds a representative minimal dataset. It used to read only the first ~100 lines of each file, which for a combined FragPipe psm.tsv (one file holding every run) kept just the first run and broke the annotation join. Files are now read in full and reduced to ~100 rows per run, so every run, Condition and replicate survives. The misleading “only the first 50 lines were loaded” warning is gone.
  • One annotation format for every search engine. read_annot() accepts a canonical Sample_folder column and derives the loader-facing aliases from it (Sample_fp verbatim, Sample_peaks with PEAKS’ hyphen/space normalization). Legacy tables providing Sample_fp or Sample_peaks load unchanged, and a user-supplied alias is never overwritten. get_annot_fragpipe()/get_annot_diann() now emit Sample_folder instead of Sample_fp (user-visible change to the generated skeleton), and PEAKS finally has a generator of its own: get_annot_peaks().
  • get_annot_sampleid() no longer fails silently: it warns when nothing matched the sample list (showing example Source_file values from both sides) and when only some rows matched (naming the dropped ones), and gained keep_all = TRUE to left-join so no annotation row is lost.
  • New tests: test-report-helpers.R; all-zero-Area coverage in test-counting.R; Sample_folder/get_annot_peaks()/get_annot_sampleid() coverage in test-annotation.R; mouse metrics in test-quality-score.R; per-run test-mode subsampling in test-loaders-fragpipe.R; single-Condition and mouse-window end-to-end renders in test-sim-fragpipe.R.

HowMaHiCo 0.14.0

  • New advanced-quantification report 06_quant_stats and its engine R/quant-stats.R: multivariate and differential statistical comparison of peptide Area between Conditions, rendered against the cached pep_all like the other focused reports. Sections: quantitative matrix and filtering summary, data completeness (per unit / per feature / presence-absence map), normalization diagnostics, dynamic range, optional imputation diagnostics, unsupervised overview (PCA scores/scree/loadings, clustered and unclustered heatmaps, PERMANOVA-style permutation test), per-contrast differential abundance (volcano, MA, p-value histogram, top-feature table), a presence/absence section for condition-exclusive ligands, a significance summary, and a “Methods & justification” section documenting every choice.
  • New exported engine functions: build_quant_matrix() (long pep_all -> feature x unit log2 matrix; Area summed over precursors on the linear scale, technical replicates averaged), filter_quant(), normalize_quant(), impute_quant(), test_differential(), test_detection(), combine_quant_results(), summarise_significant(), permanova_condition().
  • New plots: plot_completeness(), plot_missing_heatmap(), plot_intensity_dist(), plot_dynamic_range(), plot_pca(), plot_quant_heatmap() (clustered/unclustered, ggplot2 — printable inside a tabset, unlike the png-writing plot_heatmap()), plot_volcano(), plot_ma(), plot_pvalue_hist(), plot_sig_summary().
  • Two complementary missing-value tracks. limma moderated t-statistics (eBayes(trend = TRUE, robust = TRUE)) on the observed values, optionally after left-censored imputation (minprob / mindet), plus a Fisher exact test on detection counts for condition-exclusive features, whose fold change is undefined. Exclusivity is flagged by a detection-count rule rather than an FDR cut-off, because a 3-vs-3 Fisher test cannot go below p = 0.1.
  • limma is a Suggests dependency, not an Imports: it is guarded at runtime (with a BiocManager::install("limma") message) and StatMethod = "ttest" / NormMethod = "median" give a fully Bioconductor-free path, which the report falls back to automatically.
  • Fixed: run_howmahico_report("05_quality_score") was unreachable — the template was documented but missing from the function’s template choices, so match.arg() rejected it. Both 05_quality_score and 06_quant_stats are now registered, and tests/testthat/test-report-templates.R guards that every shipped template directory appears in the choices.
  • tests/testthat/test-quant-stats.R covers the engine (aggregation, filtering, normalization, imputation, limma/t-test agreement, detection test, PERMANOVA, the limma guard); test-sim-fragpipe.R renders 06_quant_stats end-to-end against the simulated FragPipe dataset.

HowMaHiCo 0.13.0

  • Pseudochromatogram coloured by density. plot_pseudochromatogram() now fills the RT bars by their own peptide count (continuous viridis gradient) instead of a flat per-Condition colour, so dense RT regions stand out within each facet.
  • New plot_pseudomobilogram() — ion-mobility analogue of the pseudochromatogram: per-Condition peptide count vs invk0 (1/k0), binned by a configurable binwidth (default 0.2), bars coloured by count. Wired into the 03_lcms_qc RT/1k0/mz view config (new “Pseudomobilograms” tab) and the 00_mhc_report distribution section (all / selected peptides).
  • Charge-proportion bars now carry a black outline (plot_charge_proportions()), matching the other stacked bar charts.
  • Peptide motifs extended to the 7–25 AA window (was capped at 24); section retitled “Peptide motifs (7 to 25 AAs)” in 01_id_counts and 00_mhc_report.
  • Subset prefix on all result files. The focused reports’ shared setup.Rmd (and the two 00_* reports) now derive a result_prefix (= Subset, or NULL when unset) and pass it to every write.csv_rawr() / write_input_params() call and the seq_by_condition.xlsx write, so result filenames carry the subset (e.g. dda_all_pep_all.csv). input_params combines the subset with the report name to stay collision-free within a shared subset subfolder.
  • tests/testthat/test-plots.R: smoke coverage for plot_pseudochromatogram() and plot_pseudomobilogram() (incl. a custom binwidth).

HowMaHiCo 0.12.0

  • 01_id_counts: new Average +/- sd per BioReplicate section mirroring the per-Condition one (mean ± SD across the TechReplicate samples within each BioReplicate). plot_count_mean_sd() gains a group_var argument (default "Condition"; pass "BioReplicate") controlling the x-axis/fill.
  • 01_id_counts: Proportion by length is now its own top-level section with Condition / BioReplicate / Sample tabs (was two nested subsections under the Total-by-Condition / Total-by-Sample sections).
  • 02_overlaps: new Overlap intra-Condition (%) section showing the replicate-overlap bars as a per-Condition percentage (stacked to 100%). plot_overlap_intra_condition() gains a value argument ("count" default, or "percent").
  • Report headers reading “Selected peptides” now show the active length window (e.g. “Selected peptides (8 to 13 AAs)”), derived from shortpep_range, across the focused templates.
  • Renamed the “Proteins” ID-level headers/labels to “Parent proteins” in the focused 01_id_counts / 02_overlaps reports (display only; the data keys and plot axis labels are unchanged).
  • tests/testthat/test-plots.R: smoke coverage for plot_count_mean_sd() (both group_var modes) and plot_overlap_intra_condition(value = "percent").

HowMaHiCo 0.11.0

  • Added a cross-class (MHC1↔︎MHC2) contamination dimension to the quality score: frac_cross_class flags MHC-II ligands co-enriched in an MHC-I pulldown (and vice versa) via their length signature — the fraction of peptides in the other class’s canonical window (MHC1 8-13, MHC2 12-25) that falls outside the current window (so the 12-13 AA overlap is handled cleanly). Scored lower_better at low weight (a small tail is biologically normal) and NA (dropped) for custom length windows. New internal helper .cross_class_range() is the single source of truth for the windows.
  • New plot plot_cross_class_length(): per-sample faceted length histogram with the cross-class region highlighted, and a matching “Cross-class contamination” section + Methods bullet in the 05_quality_score report.
  • tests/testthat/test-quality-score.R: covers .cross_class_range(), the new quality_thresholds_default() row, and frac_cross_class on an inline fixture.

HowMaHiCo 0.10.0

  • Added a per-sample immunopeptidomics quality score (inspired by the author’s HowDirty contamination score, but inverted: it scores how strongly a sample resembles a real HLA immunopeptidome rather than its contaminant load). New scoring engine in R/quality-score.R, all from the pep_all schema with no external data and no new dependency.
  • New exports: score_sample_quality() (per-sample composite + traffic-light category), qc_metrics_by_sample() (raw signals: length-window fidelity, 9-mer dominance, anchor-motif clarity, non-tryptic specificity, charge plausibility, depth, mass accuracy), anchor_information_content(), score_curve(), quality_thresholds_default(), calibrate_thresholds_from_qc(), plus plots plot_quality_heatmap() and plot_quality_composite().
  • The non-tryptic signal is deliberately low-weight and split: because some HLA-I alleles legitimately use K/R as a C-terminal anchor, the overall C-terminal K/R fraction is a low-weight diagnostic, while the scored metric isolates tryptic background in the out-of-window (long-peptide) tail.
  • Thresholds use built-in literature defaults or are calibrated from samples tagged as experiment QC controls via an optional annotation QC column (ThresholdMode = "qc_relative") — no external benchmark dataset needed. Undefined dimensions (e.g. MHC-II anchors, DIA-NN dummy ppm) drop out of the weighted composite rather than penalising the sample.
  • New focused report template 05_quality_score (inst/rmarkdown/templates/05_quality_score/): traffic-light overview, composite bar chart, per-metric breakdown and a self-documenting Methods section, rendered against the cached pep_all like the other focused reports.
  • tests/testthat/test-quality-score.R: pure-math boundary checks of score_curve() (no synthetic peptide data required).

HowMaHiCo 0.9.0

  • Added a dictionary-driven unified parser so a tabular search-engine export from a tool HowMaHiCo has no built-in loader for can be ingested by editing a YAML dictionary — no R coding, no new loader. New build_pep_all() branch software = "custom" (with a dictionary argument) routes through read_custom_batch() → parse_unified() → annotate_unified(). The dictionary maps raw → pep_all columns, sets the Found_By constant, and derives the shared recipe (Log2Area, Length_range, Nter/Cter, PeptideID, Charge formatting); per-tool transforms (unit conversions, regex extraction, accession splitting) are pre-clean responsibilities, not expressed in the dictionary.
  • New exports: read_dictionary(), parse_unified(), read_custom_batch(), annotate_unified(), and get_dictionary_template() (copies a fill-in template to the working dir, sibling of get_report_template()).
  • Shipped reference dictionaries in inst/extdata/dictionaries/ (custom_template.yaml + fragpipe.yaml / diann.yaml / peaks.yaml documenting the directly-mappable subset of each built-in loader). The three built-in loaders are unchanged.
  • tests/testthat/test-parse-unified.R: asserts parse_unified() reproduces the built-in FragPipe loader on the directly-mappable columns of the simulated dataset, plus dictionary validation and the custom build_pep_all() path.
  • New dependency: yaml (already transitive via rmarkdown).

HowMaHiCo 0.8.0

  • The four focused reports (01_id_counts, 02_overlaps, 03_lcms_qc, 04_quant) gained a PepAllSource param (with PepAllFile) selecting how to obtain pep_all: "cached" (default — load the <Subset>_pep_all.rda cache, the prior behavior), "rda" (load an explicit .rda), or "build" (parse the raw search output via build_pep_all() and write the cache). A focused report can now be rendered straight from results without a separate build_pep_all() call. Backward compatible — the default reproduces the old behavior.
  • Added a simulated FragPipe dataset (inst/extdata/sim_fragpipe_dda/, 2 Conditions x 3 BioReplicates, generated with MaHiCoInSilico) and tests/testthat/test-sim-fragpipe.R: a build_pep_all() loader assertion plus the first end-to-end render test of a focused report (gated on skip_on_cran() / pandoc). Moving the data out of data/ into inst/extdata/ also clears the R CMD check warnings about non-R files in data/.

HowMaHiCo 0.7.1

  • Fixed a “Duplicate chunk label ‘setup’” parse error that aborted every focused report (01_id_counts, 02_overlaps, 03_lcms_qc, 04_quant). The shared inst/rmarkdown/shared/setup.Rmd had a fenced r-chunk example inside its leading HTML comment; knitr parses chunk headers even inside comments, so that example re-included the file and duplicated the setup chunk. The comment now describes the include in prose, and a regression test guards against reintroducing a chunk fence there. (The two all-in-one reports were unaffected.)

HowMaHiCo 0.7.0

  • Breaking: renumbered all report templates. The template= value passed to run_howmahico_report() / get_report_template() changes: 01_mhc_report → 00_mhc_report, 02_mhc_upsets → 00_mhc_upsets, 03_id_counts → 01_id_counts, 04_overlaps → 02_overlaps, 05_lcms_qc → 03_lcms_qc, 06_quant → 04_quant. The two all-in-one reports take the 00_ prefix; the focused reports fill 01–04.
  • The LC-MS report’s “Peptide ID distribution across RT, 1/k0 and m/z” section is now generated by a single looped results='asis' chunk (a config list of the four views × the all/selected peptide sets) instead of eight hand-written chunks, matching the looped style of the motif / overlap sections.

HowMaHiCo 0.6.1

  • Moved the PTM profile from 05_lcms_qc to 03_id_counts (it is a general identification property, alongside peptide motifs), and extended it to show all peptides (pep_all) in addition to the selected-length peptides (pep_short), in an All / Selected tabset — matching the other dual sections. 05_lcms_qc now covers only the RT/1k0/mz distributions and Score/ppm QC.

HowMaHiCo 0.6.0

Multi-report framework

  • New exported build_pep_all() extracts the raw-file parsing step (the FragPipe / DIA-NN / PEAKS read → parse → annotate dispatch) into a standalone, unit-tested function that writes the <Subset>_pep_all.rda cache. Run it once, then render any of the focused reports against that cache instead of re-parsing the raw search files per report.
  • Four new focused report templates, each a slice of the all-in-one 01_mhc_report, rendered the same way via run_howmahico_report():
    • 03_id_counts — total IDs, identification counts (mean±sd, by length, by charge, by sample), peptide size distributions, peptide motifs.
    • 04_overlaps — intra-Condition replicate overlap, UpSet across Conditions, and Condition pairwise overlap.
    • 05_lcms_qc — RT / 1k0 / m/z distributions, Score and mass-error identification QC, and the PTM profile (advanced LC-MS QC).
    • 06_quant — log2(Area) correlation and Area %CV violins.
  • The focused reports share one setup fragment (inst/rmarkdown/shared/setup.Rmd, pulled in via a knitr child) that loads the cache and derives the common objects, instead of duplicating the boilerplate in every skeleton.
  • 01_mhc_report and 02_mhc_upsets are unchanged — full retrocompatibility.

HowMaHiCo 0.5.0

Report: per-length splits for the overlap and charge sections

  • plot_overlap_intra_condition() now returns a single replicate-overlap bar chart for one data frame and one ID level, instead of stacking all-vs-selected peptides into a two-row ggpubr::ggarrange(). Breaking signature change: the arguments are now (df, id_col, title = NULL, shortpep_range) (previously (pep_all, pep_short, id_col, shortpep_range)). The main report’s “Overlap intra-Condition” section now presents All peptides and Selected peptides as separate nested tabsets (Peptides / Sequences / Proteins), matching the “Average +/- sd” section.
  • The “Peptides identified per charge +1 to +4” section now renders a plot for the selected-length peptides (pep_short) alongside the all-peptides plot, in an All peptides / Selected peptides tabset. The selected-length plot is also written out when PlotsSave = TRUE.

HowMaHiCo 0.4.0

Loader consistency & portability

  • Unified Log2Area zero-handling across all three loaders: a zero Area/Intensity now maps to NA everywhere. Previously FragPipe and DIA-NN mapped it to 1 while PEAKS mapped it to NA, so the same zero-area row behaved differently depending on the search engine. This changes FragPipe/DIA-NN output for zero-area rows — they no longer carry a fabricated Log2Area = 1. The shared logic now lives in an internal compute_log2area() helper.
  • Run-name extraction (DIA-NN File.Name, Bruker HyStar Result.Path) is now separator-agnostic via an internal extract_run_name() helper, replacing a backslash-anchored regex that only worked on Windows-style paths. The loaders are now portable to Linux/macOS (and Docker).
  • Each parse_*() validates its output against the core pep_all schema (validate_pep_all()), so a loader that drops/renames a core column or returns an empty table fails loudly at the source instead of producing a half-broken report several sections later.

Report robustness & provenance

  • The main report (01_mhc_report) no longer aborts on partial subsets: the UpSet sections skip gracefully when fewer than two Conditions are present, and the Area %CV sections render an explanatory note instead of erroring when no replicates exist.
  • Both report templates gained a “Session & provenance” footer: the run parameters as a table, the package version, and a collapsible sessionInfo(), so a saved HTML is self-documenting.
  • Declared the previously-undeclared DataAcquisitionNames parameter in the 02_mhc_upsets template (it was referenced in the header but never defined in the YAML, so it rendered blank).

HowMaHiCo 0.3.0

Packaging & best-practices cleanup

  • Declared the previously-undeclared base-package dependencies (grDevices, graphics, stats, utils) in DESCRIPTION Imports.
  • The full exported function set is now part of the public reference: removed @keywords internal from every exported function (the package-overview page and the non-exported helpers stay internal), and listed every export in _pkgdown.yml.
  • All package R code — both the R/ source and the two report templates (inst/rmarkdown/templates/*/skeleton/skeleton.Rmd) — now uses the native R pipe (|>) throughout instead of magrittr %>%. This raises the minimum R version to 4.1.0 (Depends: R (>= 4.1.0)).
  • De-vendored get_dirs_index_peaks(): the helper (originally adapted from deltaProtR) is now native HowMaHiCo code in R/loaders-peaks-dirs.R (was R/vendored-deltaprotr.R).
  • Added this NEWS.md changelog.

Bug fixes

  • check_file_exists() now names the conflicting file in its error/warning message (the filename was previously printed after stop(), so it never appeared).
  • check_output_exists() no longer lists upset_table_prot.csv twice.
  • The log2(Area) heatmap “saved in” message now reports the actual output path instead of a hardcoded 4_figures/... string.

HowMaHiCo 0.2.1

  • Peptide motifs (seqlogo) now shown up to length 24 (was 22).
  • Identification counts “Average ± sd” split into per-length individual plots and nested tabsets, with all-peptides vs selected-peptides shown separately.
  • “Peptide ID distribution across RT, 1/k0 and m/z” refactored out of the template into plot_pseudochromatogram() and plot_2d_distribution().
  • Replaced hardcoded scale_y_continuous() breaks/labels with n.breaks = 5 in plot_bp_count_length(), plot_count_mean_sd(), and plot_overlap_intra_condition().
  • Homogenized bar alpha = 0.7 and added black outlines across plot functions.
  • Fixed count_ids_condition_bylengthrange() dropping an existing Condition column before renaming.

HowMaHiCo 0.2.0

  • Completed Phases 1–6 of the conversion into a proper R package: functions moved into R/, report templates shipped under inst/rmarkdown/templates/{01_mhc_report,02_mhc_upsets}/, a testthat (edition 3) suite, roxygen man/ pages, _pkgdown.yml, and CI (R-CMD-check + pkgdown).
  • Added a proportion-by-length plot at the sample level to the “Total by Sample” section.
  • plot_peplength_hist() density normalized by condition total rather than per-group.

HowMaHiCo 0.1.4

  • Fixed rendered output_file landing in the installed package library instead of the working directory.

HowMaHiCo 0.1.3

  • Named all report chunks and unified fig.width = 8 across chunks.
  • Added plot_peplength_hist() (a simpler length-distribution histogram without the boxplot overlay, facetable, two-color by MHCclass, density or absolute).

HowMaHiCo 0.1.2

  • Introduced theme_howmahico() and applied it across plot functions and report skeletons.
  • MHCclass parameter with default length windows (MHC1: 8–13 AA, MHC2: 12–25 AA) and a manual color/fill palette per class.
  • Added a pre-flight check that every file named in the annotation table exists, a per-sample “Total by Sample” section, and a programmatically generated report title.

HowMaHiCo 0.1.1

  • Suppressed the progress bar in get_annot_diann().

HowMaHiCo 0.1.0

  • First package-shaped release. Renamed the report templates to 01_mhc_report and 02_mhc_upsets; split read_peaks_batch() into read/parse/annotate matching the FragPipe/DIA-NN loader families; batch readers now read only the files referenced in the annotation table.
